examples.text: “Who calls, who calls?” cried Essper; a shout was the only answer. There was no path, but the underwood was low, and Vivian took his horse, an old forester, across it with ease. Essper’s jibbed.
examples.ref: 1826, Benjamin Disraeli, Vivian Grey, London: Henry Colburn, published 1827, Volume 4, Book 6, page 73:

examples.text: Then he got fever, and had to be carried in a hammock slung under a pole. As he weighed sixteen stone I had no end of rows with the carriers. They jibbed, ran away, sneaked off with their loads in the night—quite a mutiny.
examples.ref: 1899 February, Joseph Conrad, “The Heart of Darkness”, in Blackwood’s Edinburgh Magazine, volume CLXV, number M, New York, N.Y.: The Leonard Scott Publishing Company, […], →OCLC, part I:

examples.text: The lama jibbed at the open door of a crowded third-class carriage. ‘Were it not better to walk?’ said he weakly.
"Where are we going?" she asked, jibbing capriciously in the descent.
examples.ref: 1930, Norman Lindsay, Redheap, Sydney, N.S.W.: Ure Smith, →OCLC, page 119:

examples.text: “Juno has a kindly gait. She neither jibs nor shies, though she will take a fence no more. […]”

glosses: To stop and refuse to go forward (usually of a horse).

examples.text: “What say you to the young lady herself?” said Craigengelt; “the finest young woman in all Scotland, one that you used to be so fond of when she was cross, and now she consents to have you, and gives up her engagement with Ravenswood, you are for jibbing. I must say, the devil’s in ye, when ye neither know what you would have nor what you would want.”
examples.ref: 1819, Walter Scott, chapter 28, in The Bride of Lammermoor:

examples.text: I hadn't much chance of buying a practice or dropping into a partnership worth having and I jibbed at setting up in some God-forsaken backwater and slipping into middle age 'building up a connection.'
examples.ref: 1923, Ernest Bramah, The Eyes of Max Carrados:

examples.text: Some of us began to jib when the family began to collect portraits of their new son to decorate their walls […].
